REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - JUNE 26, 2025 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.gov in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

Report from City Manager/Executive Director
During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, verbal reports will also be provided in such cases where the City Council-appointed delegate and/or alternate is unable to attend a scheduled meeting, and there is insufficient time to schedule an agenda item for Council consideration of another alternate, necessitating a Mayor's urgency appointment. Requests may also be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item, except to cancel or reschedule a City Council public meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY, JUNE 26, 2025,
7:00 PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

  1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

  2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Rob Golding, First Christian Reformed Church.

  3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by the 2025 BASES Program – Juarez Elementary
  School.

  4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jennifer Hong
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Council/Agency Member Sophia M. Tse
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Lynda P. Johnson
  Mayor/Chair Frank Aurelio Yokoyama

  5.  Presentations/Appointments

  5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council honoring:

  Asha, Ayanna Esther, and Acacia Ann Greenidge; and Yolanda Williams, President, Pi
  Sigma Omega, a chapter of the Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority (Juneteenth Recognition).

  Antonio Lavermon, LGBTQ+ Program Facilitator and Liaison, Cerritos College (Pride
  Month Recognition).

  The White Lotus Florist (Business Spotlight).

  5B.  An informational report and overview of the services provided by the Greater Los Angeles
  County Vector Control District.

  Informational reports were given by Mark Bollman, Board of Trustees Member (Cerritos
  representative), and Caroline Gongora, Public Information Coordinator, of the Greater Los
  Angeles County Vector Control District. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  There was no action taken on this item.

  6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for items not listed on the meeting
  agenda but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the
  Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, June 26, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 13

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Howard Sachs expressed concern regarding management at the Ivy Park at Cerritos
  facility.

  Melissa Meng, Summer Intern for Assemblywoman Sharon Quirk-Silva, spoke regarding
  State Assembly events and services.

  Daryl Terrell expressed concern regarding catalytic converter theft and requested the
  City adopt an ordinance prohibiting the unlawful possession of a catalytic converter.

  CONSENSUS (Yokoyama): Directed the City Manager to conduct research regarding a
  potential ordinance prohibiting the unlawful possession of a catalytic converter, inclusive
  of an existing such ordinance in the City of Artesia.

  Gabriel Abboud expressed concern regarding recent U.S. Immigration and Customs
  Enforcement (ICE) local activity.

  Mel Cortez spoke in support of increased community involvement in Neighborhood Watch
  programs.

  Case van der Linden expressed concern regarding watering of newly planted parkway
  trees and requested the City implement programs similar to those in the cities of
  Hawaiian Gardens and Cypress.

  Sam Desai requested the City Council remove agenda Item 7D from the Consent
  Calendar for separate consideration and spoke in support of the Cerritos Regional
  Chamber of Commerce. He also thanked the City Council for recently increasing public
  comment time limits and expressed concern regarding the length of Council meetings.

  Norma Williamson expressed gratitude for additional pickleball court installation at
  Cerritos Park East and Liberty Park and spoke regarding upcoming Neighborhood Watch
  events.

  Teddy Lloyd offered various suggestions for potential revenue-generating opportunities
  for the City.

  Jill Nishida expressed concern regarding the recent voter adoption of Measure J, setting
  the Cerritos General Municipal Election date in the City Charter; support for placement of
  a measure on the next Cerritos election ballot to request voter consideration of changing
  the general municipal election dates to even-numbered years; concern regarding the
  cancellation of upcoming City events; and gratitude for the “From the Mayor’s Desk”
  weekly column.

  Kirit Chauhan expressed gratitude for additional pickleball court installation at Cerritos
  Park East; support for placement of a measure on the next Cerritos election ballot, to
  request voter consideration of changing the general municipal election dates to even-
  numbered years; and concern regarding misinformation and recent U.S. Immigration and
  Customs Enforcement (ICE) local activity.

  Susan Green expressed concern regarding the City adopting sister cities in the Philippines
  and requested consideration for other cultures/communities.

  Mark Bryan expressed concern regarding potential closure of the Cerritos Library one (1)
  day per week.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, June 26, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 13

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  The Mayor announced that prior to the meeting, the Council/Agency members received
  full-text, unredacted copies of the two (2) written comments submitted for Item 6, by
  the deadline listed on the agenda and for inclusion in the official record. Requests for
  copies of the written comments submitted for this meeting can be made during regular

  AGREEMENT FOR THE LOS ANGELES GATEWAY REGION INTEGRATED REGIONAL WATER

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Tse, to:

  1.  Waive full reading and adopt, Resolution No. 2025-18, A RESOLUTION OF

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Approval of an amendment to increase Purchase Order No. 125006 to add a sewer rate
  study to the existing scope of services (COUNCIL).

  This item was pulled from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration, by
  Councilmember Hong.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments period.

  Sam Desai expressed concern regarding City Council approval of this item and requested
  further explanation and community education efforts related to utility rate adjustments.

  Kirit Chauhan expressed support for City Council approval of this item and the
  promulgation of a master plan.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period and public
  hearing closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:

  1. Approve the proposed amendment to increase Purchase Order No. 125006 by
  $34,595 for a new total amount of $83,100 to complete the existing water rate study
  and include the proposed sewer rate study; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager or designee to execute contract amendments, provided
  that the total cumulative increase does not exceed $50,000 or 15% of the original
  contract value, whichever is greater (COUNCIL).
